To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the emotional context modulates touch perception at two stages: anticipation and interpretation; (2) the early somatosensory potentials (SEPs), which reflect the tactile sensation, are amplified after angry, sad and happy facial expressions; (3) the late SEPs, which reflect the interpretation of touch, are attenuated after happy and amplified after anger.

the emotional expressions of a toucher modulate the sensory processing of touch, and the modulation takes place as early as 20–30 ms after the onset of touch, which suggests that emotion may affect the tactile perception before the sensory signals reach the primary somatosensory cortex.
the affective modulation of tactile perception occurs at two levels: anticipation and interpretation, which is indexed by early and late components of the somatosensory evoked potentials.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of emotion in tactile perception.
the role of emotional context on the perception of touch.
the relationship between the perception of touch and the emotional context in which touch occurs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the emotional context affects the tactile sensation, but not in a straightforward manner.
the emotional modulation of touch is a dynamic and continuous process.
the emotional expressions of the toucher affect the sensory perception of the toucher, which may be due to the anticipation and interpretation processes of the toucher.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the touch experience is not just the sensory information from skin, but the emotional information from social context.
emotional expressions modulate touch perception at different temporal ranges, which may provide a new perspective to investigate the relationship between touch and emotion.
emotional expressions can alter tactile sensation, which in turn may affect our social behavior and social cognition.
The main takeaway from our work is that

emotional modulation of tactile processing is not limited to the cognitive level, and the emotional modulation of touch is a two-stage process, with an initial anticipation phase, followed by an interpretation phase.
touch is not only affected by the emotional context of the situation, but also the emotional expressions of the toucher.
touch perception is not only affected by the emotional context, but the emotional context is also affected by the touch.
